In the film, Bond has retired from active service in MI6 and is recruited by the [CIA](/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency") to extract a kidnapped scientist carrying deadly DNA-targeting nanobots, leading him to uncover a plot by the bioterrorist Lyutsifer Safin to kill millions of people. The film was directed by [Cary Joji Fukunaga](/wiki/Cary_Joji_Fukunaga "Cary Joji Fukunaga") from a screenplay he co-wrote with [Neal Purvis, Robert Wade](/wiki/Neal_Purvis_and_Robert_Wade "Neal Purvis and Robert Wade") and [Phoebe Waller-Bridge](/wiki/Phoebe_Waller-Bridge "Phoebe Waller-Bridge"), based on a story conceived by Purvis, Wade and Fukunaga. In addition to Craig, [Léa Seydoux](/wiki/L%C3%A9a_Seydoux "Léa Seydoux"), [Ben Whishaw](/wiki/Ben_Whishaw "Ben Whishaw"), [Naomie Harris](/wiki/Naomie_Harris "Naomie Harris"), [Jeffrey Wright](/wiki/Jeffrey_Wright "Jeffrey Wright"), [Christoph Waltz](/wiki/Christoph_Waltz "Christoph Waltz"), [Ralph Fiennes](/wiki/Ralph_Fiennes "Ralph Fiennes"), and [Rory Kinnear](/wiki/Rory_Kinnear "Rory Kinnear") reprise their roles from previous films, with [Rami Malek](/wiki/Rami_Malek "Rami Malek"), [Lashana Lynch](/wiki/Lashana_Lynch "Lashana Lynch"), [Billy Magnussen](/wiki/Billy_Magnussen "Billy Magnussen"), [Ana de Armas](/wiki/Ana_de_Armas "Ana de Armas"), [David Dencik](/wiki/David_Dencik "David Dencik"), and [Dali Benssalah](/wiki/Dali_Benssalah "Dali Benssalah") appearing in new roles.

fanoutqa_029905.x:
Stay (The Kid Laroi and Justin Bieber song) :: Background :: chunk_0001
On 20 September 2020, Laroi shared a snippet of the song on an [Instagram](/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") live stream, followed by a longer snippet in better quality that was previewed on a live stream from Rolling Loud on 29 October 2020. Bieber's contribution to the song was revealed on 31 May 2021. The song leaked in full on a [Discord](/wiki/Discord_(software) "Discord (software)") server on 2 June 2021.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

"Stay" marks Laroi's first major single release as a lead artist in 2021 and Bieber's first major single as a lead artist since the release of his second extended play, *[Freedom](/wiki/Freedom_(EP) "Freedom (EP)")*, which was released in April 2021. On 3 June 2021, [Scooter Braun](/wiki/Scooter_Braun "Scooter Braun"), who has been Bieber's manager from the start of his career, also became Laroi's manager, until Laroi left and joined [Adam Leber](/wiki/Adam_Leber "Adam Leber") at Rebel Management on 27 September 2021.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

Laroi had the song for about a year before its release. He created the song while spending time with producers [Charlie Puth](/wiki/Charlie_Puth "Charlie Puth"), [Omer Fedi](/wiki/Omer_Fedi "Omer Fedi"), and [Blake Slatkin](/wiki/Blake_Slatkin "Blake Slatkin") at Slatkin's house. Puth played the melody of the song on the keyboard, but Laroi ended up liking it and wanted to get it in production software [Pro Tools](/wiki/Pro_Tools "Pro Tools") to use it to create a song. He felt that "it was probably the most organic way of making a song I've ever done – ever". Laroi thought Bieber "would sound perfect", so he went to the studio at which Bieber records; they finished recording the song, but Bieber was hesitant about whether his vocals sounded good or not.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

Main article: [Energy in the United Arab Emirates](/wiki/Energy_in_the_United_Arab_Emirates "Energy in the United Arab Emirates")

See also: [Solar power in the United Arab Emirates](/wiki/Solar_power_in_the_United_Arab_Emirates "Solar power in the United Arab Emirates")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/ADNOC_Refining_Ruwais_Site-187.jpg/250px-ADNOC_Refining_Ruwais_Site-187.jpg)](/wiki/File:ADNOC_Refining_Ruwais_Site-187.jpg)

[Ruwais Refinery](/wiki/Ruwais_Refinery "Ruwais Refinery") is the fourth-largest single-site oil refinery in the world and the biggest in the Middle East.

Oil and gas production is an important part of the economy of the UAE. In 2018, the oil and gas sector contributed 26% to overall GDP. The UAE leadership initiated economic diversification efforts even before the oil price crash in the 1980s, resulting in the UAE having the most diversified economy in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region at present. Although the oil and gas sector continues to be significant to the UAE economy, these efforts have yielded great resilience during periods of oil price fluctuations and economic turbulence. The introduction of the VAT has provided the government with an additional source of income – approximately 6% of the total revenue in 2018, or 27 billion [United Arab Emirates dirham](/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_dirham "United Arab Emirates dirham") (AED) – affording its fiscal policy more independence from oil- and gas-related revenue, which constitutes about 36% of the total government revenue.

The [Barakah nuclear power plant](/wiki/Barakah_nuclear_power_plant "Barakah nuclear power plant") is the first on the Arabian peninsula and expected to reduce the carbon footprint of the country.[[294]](#cite_note-298)

The UAE has solar generation potential, and its energy policy has shifted due to the declining price of solar. The Dubai Clean Energy Strategy aims to provide 7 per cent of Dubai's energy from clean energy sources by 2020. It will increase this target to 25 per cent by 2030 and 75 per cent by 2050.[[295]](#cite_note-299)

*Noble gas* is translated from the [German](/wiki/German_language "German language") noun *Edelgas*, first used in 1900 by [Hugo Erdmann](/wiki/Hugo_Erdmann "Hugo Erdmann")[[5]](#cite_note-5) to indicate their extremely low level of reactivity. The name makes an analogy to the term "[noble metals](/wiki/Noble_metal "Noble metal")", which also have low reactivity. The noble gases have also been referred to as *[inert gases](/wiki/Inert_gas "Inert gas")*, but this label is deprecated as many [noble gas compounds](/wiki/Noble_gas_compound "Noble gas compound") are now known.[[6]](#cite_note-6) *Rare gases* is another term that was used,[[7]](#cite_note-7) but this is also inaccurate because [argon](/wiki/Argon "Argon") forms a fairly considerable part (0.94% by volume, 1.3% by mass) of the [Earth's atmosphere](/wiki/Earth%27s_atmosphere "Earth's atmosphere") due to decay of radioactive [potassium-40](/wiki/Potassium-40 "Potassium-40").[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Thanks to its characteristic [spectral lines](/wiki/Spectral_line "Spectral line"), [Helium](/wiki/Helium "Helium") was discovered to exist on the Sun before it was discovered on Earth.

[Pierre Janssen](/wiki/Pierre_Janssen "Pierre Janssen") and [Joseph Norman Lockyer](/wiki/Joseph_Norman_Lockyer "Joseph Norman Lockyer") had discovered a new element on 18 August 1868 while looking at the [chromosphere](/wiki/Chromosphere "Chromosphere") of the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun"), and named it [helium](/wiki/Helium "Helium") after the Greek word for the Sun, ἥλιος (*hḗlios*).[[9]](#cite_note-9) No chemical analysis was possible at the time, but helium was later found to be a noble gas. Drinking may be a cause of earlier onset of [colorectal](/wiki/Colorectal "Colorectal") cancer.[[63]](#cite_note-63) The evidence that alcohol is a cause of bowel cancer is convincing in men and probable in women.[[64]](#cite_note-64)

The National Institutes of Health,[[65]](#cite_note-65) the National Cancer Institute,[[66]](#cite_note-66) Cancer Research,[[67]](#cite_note-67) the American Cancer Society,[[68]](#cite_note-68) the Mayo Clinic,[[69]](#cite_note-69) and the Colorectal Cancer Coalition,[[70]](#cite_note-70) American Society of Clinical Oncology[[71]](#cite_note-71) and the Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center[[72]](#cite_note-72) list alcohol as a risk factor.

A WCRF panel report finds the evidence "convincing" that alcoholic drinks increase the risk of colorectal cancer in men at consumption levels above 30 grams of absolute alcohol daily.[[73]](#cite_note-WCRF-73) The [National Cancer Institute](/wiki/National_Cancer_Institute "National Cancer Institute") states, "Heavy alcohol use may also increase the risk of colorectal cancer"[[74]](#cite_note-74)

A 2011 meta-analysis found that alcohol consumption was associated with an increased risk of colorectal cancer.[[75]](#cite_note-75)

Coach [Don Feeley](/wiki/Don_Feeley "Don Feeley"), formerly the basketball coach at [Fairleigh Dickinson University](/wiki/Fairleigh_Dickinson_University "Fairleigh Dickinson University") in [New Jersey](/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey"), traveled to Sudan to coach and held clinics for the Sudanese national team in 1982. Feeley convinced Bol to go to the United States and play basketball.[[19]](#cite_note-20)[[20]](#cite_note-auto1-21)

With Feeley's input, Bol first landed in [Cleveland](/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland"). According to [Cleveland State University](/wiki/Cleveland_State_University "Cleveland State University") basketball coach [Kevin Mackey](/wiki/Kevin_Mackey "Kevin Mackey"), Bol could not provide a record of his birth date.[[7]](#cite_note-Yahoo_Birthdate-8) Mackey listed it as October 16, 1962, on Cleveland State documents, making Bol 19 years old, but he believed Bol was actually much older, possibly as old as 35.[[7]](#cite_note-Yahoo_Birthdate-8) Bol did not speak or write English at the time of his arrival in Cleveland. He improved his English skills after months of classes at ESL Language Centers at [Case Western Reserve University](/wiki/Case_Western_Reserve_University "Case Western Reserve University"), but not enough to qualify for enrollment at Cleveland State. Bol never played a game for Cleveland State. Five years later, Cleveland State was placed on two years' probation for providing improper financial assistance to Bol and two other African players.[[21]](#cite_note-22)[[22]](#cite_note-auto2-23)

Again with Feeley's influence, Bol declared his intention to play professionally in the [National Basketball Association](/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA). The [San Diego Clippers](/wiki/Los_Angeles_Clippers "Los Angeles Clippers") drafted him in the [1983 NBA draft](/wiki/1983_NBA_draft "1983 NBA draft") as the 97th overall pick. Clippers head coach [Jim Lynam](/wiki/Jim_Lynam "Jim Lynam") received a call about Bol from Feeley, whom he knew from coaching circles. "So, I said, 'Have you told anyone else about this?'" Lynam recalled.

[Twenty-four U.S. astronauts](/wiki/List_of_Apollo_astronauts "List of Apollo astronauts") traveled to the Moon's vicinity under the Apollo program. Virginia has ranked near the top of collegiate athletics programs in recent years.
